- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed — apply a 2–3% downward bias if sentiment is >0.5 in 3 consecutive days.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive drops >1.5% from prior day), model often lags — adjust forecast to match recent 5-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., >2% in 1–2 days), model often fails to anticipate — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days if sentiment remains high.
